ev.q: Age- and sex-standardized prevalence of reporting ever having experienced Long COVID among Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System survey respondents
The weighted age- and sex-standardized prevalence ranged from 1.9% (95% CI = 0.9%–4.1%) for the U.S. Virgin Islands to 10.6% (95% CI = 9.5%–11.8%) for West Virginia
Nationally, 6.4% of noninstitutionalized U.S. adults reported ever having experienced Long COVID
ranged from 1.9% (95% CI = 0.9%–4.1%) for the U.S. Virgin Islands to 10.6% (95% CI = 9.5%–11.8%) for West Virginia
Estimates were standardized to the 2020 U.S. Census Bureau population of noninstitutionalized, civilian adults.

methods_quotes.q: CDC estimated weighted age- and sex-standardized prevalence with a 95% CI of ever having experienced Long COVID
Estimates were standardized to the 2020 U.S. Census Bureau population of noninstitutionalized, civilian adults.
Analyses were conducted using SAS-callable SUDAAN (version 9.4; RTI International) and account for complex survey design.
Prevalence estimates were divided into quintiles.
